findings.title: Quiz JSON is cast to QuizQuestion[] with no runtime guard, then persisted to IndexedDB as ReviewCards
findings.description: `JSON.parse(...) as { questions?: QuizQuestion[] }` is a pure assertion over non-deterministic model output. `QuizQuestion` (src/types.ts:105-110) declares `question`, `options`, `correctAnswerIndex` and `explanation` as REQUIRED, so after the cast TypeScript swears every element is complete. Nothing at runtime checks that. The `?? []` on line 17 only covers a null/undefined `questions` key — it does not check that `questions` is an array, nor that any element has the four fields. Contrast schemas.ts:85-97, where the book response deliberately gets a `Raw*` all-optional mirror type; that discipline was not applied to quiz or recommendations, so these two reuse the strict domain types directly. Concrete failure: QuizModal.tsx:50-61 iterates the parsed array and calls `reviewCards.upsert(newCard({ options: question.options, correctAnswerIndex: question.correctAnswerIndex, ... }))`, writing a `ReviewCard` straight into the IndexedDB `reviewCards` store. A model that omits `options` persists `options: undefined`. ReviewPage.tsx:93 then does `current.options.map(...)` on the earliest-due card and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`, taking the whole /review route to the error boundary. There is NO recovery: `reviewCards` in src/lib/storage/repo.ts:77-109 exposes only `listByProfile`, `listDue`, `listByBook`, `upsert` and `removeByBook` — there is no per-card delete and no re-validation on read, so the only escape is deleting the entire book. A non-array `questions` value is equally unguarded: `setQuestions(quizData)` runs before the `for...of` throws, so the render path hits `questions[i].question` on `undefined`. Correct behavior: parse into `unknown`, validate each element with a type guard (or an all-optional `RawQuizResponse` mirror plus a filter), and drop malformed questions before they reach storage. Blast radius: 1 direct call site (QuizModal.tsx:44), but the corrupted records fan out to the entire review feature (ReviewPage, useReviewQueue, stats). Zero test coverage — src/lib/ai has only apiKey.test.ts and errors.test.ts.

findings.title: The Gemini responseSchema objects are the only shape enforcement and receive zero compile-time checking
findings.description: All three schema constants are bare object literals with no type annotation and no `satisfies Schema`. They are passed to `config.responseSchema`, whose declared type in the SDK is `SchemaUnion` — and `node_modules/@google/genai/dist/genai.d.ts:12090` declares `export declare type SchemaUnion = Schema | unknown;`, which collapses to `unknown`. So the compiler accepts literally any value there. Because the constants are assigned to untyped `const`s first, object-literal freshness is lost and excess-property checking never applies at the call site either. Net effect: a typo (`requred` instead of `required`, `properites` instead of `properties`), a misplaced `description`, or a nested `items` on a non-ARRAY field compiles cleanly, ships, and silently degrades the request to an unconstrained one. That matters more here than anywhere else in the app: with no runtime validation on any of the three parse sites (L05-F01, L05-F04, L05-F05), this schema is the *sole* thing keeping model output in shape. The SDK's `Schema` interface (genai.d.ts:12043-12088) is a real, checkable type with `properties?: Record<string, Schema>`, `required?: string[]`, `items?: Schema`, `enum?: string[]`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `minItems`/`maxItems` — annotating each constant `satisfies Schema` is a trivial, zero-runtime-cost fix that would catch the whole class. Blast radius: 3 schemas consumed by 4 request sites (summarize.ts:49, summarize.ts:70, quiz.ts:13, recommend.ts:27). Verified negative worth recording: `GENERIC_BOOK_SCHEMA`'s 9 properties and `RawBookResponse`'s 9 fields match exactly with no drift in either direction.

findings.title: `response.text || '{}'` erases a blocked or truncated completion, fabricating a complete-looking Book that gets persisted
findings.description: The SDK types the accessor as `get text(): string | undefined` (genai.d.ts:5338). `undefined` is the real signal for a safety-blocked prompt, a `MAX_TOKENS` truncation, or an empty `candidates` array. `|| '{}'` coerces that signal away — and unlike a `!`, it fails silently instead of throwing. The empty object then flows through `toGenerated` (lines 22-41), where every field has a fallback: `data.title || fallbackTitle`, `data.category || 'Other'`, `data.rating ?? 0`, `data.readingTimeMinutes ?? 5`, `'No takeaway available.'`, `'No summary available.'`, `keyInsights: []`, `actionableSteps: []`. The function returns a structurally perfect `GeneratedBook` and its type promises a real generated summary. LibraryPage.tsx:90-94 then writes that straight to IndexedDB via `addBook`, and AddBookModal.tsx:69-79 does the same. The user asked for a summary, Gemini refused, and BookSum silently saves a book whose summary reads 'No summary available.' with an empty insights list — with no error surfaced anywhere (the catch on line 55 never fires). `'{}'` is also indistinguishable from the model legitimately returning `{}`. Correct behavior: treat `response.text === undefined` (or an empty/blocked `candidates[0]`) as an `AiError` of kind `'safety'` or `'malformed'` — `src/lib/ai/errors.ts:1-9` already has both kinds and user-facing copy for them (errors.ts:33,35), so nothing new needs designing. Same pattern at line 73 for the PDF path, quiz.ts:16 and recommend.ts:30. Blast radius: 4 parse sites; 2 UI entry points persist the result.

findings.title: Recommendations cast to a required-field type with no guard; a missing title throws inside the cover fallback and loses all six results
findings.description: `as { recommendations?: Omit<Recommendation, 'coverUrl'>[] }` asserts that every element has non-optional `title`, `author` and `description` (declared at recommend.ts:9-14). Nothing validates that. `?? []` on line 35 guards only a null/undefined `recommendations` key, not a non-array value and not element shape. Two concrete failures. (1) A model that omits `title` on one recommendation: `fetchCover(rec.title, rec.author)` receives `undefined`. src/lib/covers/index.ts:13-20 swallows lookup errors, but its final line 21 `return placeholderCover(title)` is OUTSIDE the try, and placeholder.ts:5 calls `title.trim()` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'trim')`. Because the map is wrapped in `Promise.all`, one bad element rejects the whole batch, the catch on line 40 converts it via `toAiError` into the generic 'Something went wrong talking to Gemini' (errors.ts:36 — a `TypeError` whose message lacks 'fetch' falls through to `'unknown'`), and all six recommendations are lost with a misleading message. (2) `recommendations` returned as an object rather than an array: `.map is not a function`, same misleading error. Even when nothing throws, an `undefined` field is spread into the `Recommendation` and cached — LibraryPage.tsx:74-77 writes the array to `localStorage`, and LibraryPage.tsx:35 re-asserts it back as `Recommendation[]` on the next load with no validation, so the bad shape survives reloads. Correct behavior: define an all-optional `RawRecommendationResponse` mirror (matching the existing `RawBookResponse` pattern in schemas.ts:87) and filter out elements missing a title/author before calling `fetchCover`. Blast radius: 1 call site (LibraryPage.tsx:71), whose output reaches localStorage and RecommendationCarousel.

findings.title: `?? []` / `|| 'fallback'` in toGenerated guard only nullish values, so a wrong-typed field is persisted and crashes every later read
findings.description: `RawBookResponse` is honest about optionality (schemas.ts:85-97 correctly marks every field `?`), but the coercions in `toGenerated` only defend against `null`/`undefined`. `data.keyInsights ?? []` passes a *string* straight through, and the assertion at line 52 means TypeScript never complains. The result is assigned to `Summary.keyInsights` which src/types.ts:59 declares as `string[]` — a lying type on a record that is written durably to IndexedDB by AddBookModal.tsx:78 and LibraryPage.tsx:93. Nothing re-validates on read. Every later consumer assumes the array: prompts.ts:36 `summary.keyInsights.join('\n')` (deep-dive generation), prompts.ts:67 and prompts.ts:70 (chat system instruction), prompts.ts:82 (audio script), plus `.map` in BookDetail. All throw `TypeError: ... .join is not a function` — so a single malformed generation permanently breaks chat, audio and deep-dive for that book. Same exposure on `actionableSteps` (line 37). Likelihood is lower than the missing-field cases because Gemini structured output usually honours ARRAY, but the cost is durable corruption and the guard is one `Array.isArray` per field. Correct behavior: validate with `Array.isArray(x) && x.every(i => typeof i === 'string')` before constructing the `Summary`, or run the parsed object through a guard function that returns `RawBookResponse | null`. Blast radius: both `summarizeBook` and `summarizePdf` funnel through `toGenerated`; 3 UI call sites persist its output.

findings.title: generateDetailedSummary returns a failure sentinel typed as `string`, which callers persist as a real summary
findings.description: The declared return `Promise<string>` makes success and failure structurally identical — the caller cannot tell 'the model produced this markdown' from 'generation produced nothing'. `text` is empty whenever the stream yields no chunks: a safety block, an immediate `MAX_TOKENS` cut, or an empty candidate list (chunk.text is `string | undefined` per genai.d.ts:9465, and line 95 already coalesces it to ''). The sentinel is not just cosmetic — BookDetail.tsx:184-186 does `const longSummary = await generateDetailedSummary(...); const updated = { ...summary, detailedSummary: longSummary }; onSummaryUpdate(updated);`, persisting the literal string 'Failed to generate detailed summary.' into `Summary.detailedSummary` in IndexedDB. BookDetail.tsx:176 then short-circuits on `if (summary?.detailedSummary)` and opens the reader without regenerating, so from that point on the 'Read Full Summary' button permanently opens a reader displaying the failure message, with no UI path to retry. The catch on line 188 never fires because nothing threw. Correct shape: either throw an `AiError` (kind `'malformed'` or `'safety'` already exist in errors.ts:1-9) when `text` is empty, or return a tagged union (`{ ok: true; text: string } | { ok: false; reason: AiErrorKind }`) so the compiler forces the caller to handle the empty case before writing to storage. Blast radius: 1 call site (BookDetail.tsx:184), but the bad value is durable and self-perpetuating.

findings.title: QUIZ_SCHEMA leaves correctAnswerIndex as NUMBER and options unbounded, so the only enforcement layer permits ungradeable quizzes
findings.description: `correctAnswerIndex` is declared `Type.NUMBER` even though the SDK exposes `Type.INTEGER` (genai.d.ts:14295) and the field is an array index; the 0-3 range lives only in a `description` string, which is a prompt hint, not a constraint. `Schema` supports `minimum`/`maximum` (genai.d.ts:12064,12072) and `minItems`/`maxItems` (12059,12067) and none are used. On the TS side `QuizQuestion.correctAnswerIndex` (src/types.ts:108) and `ReviewCard.correctAnswerIndex` (src/types.ts:89) are plain `number`, so nothing at either layer rejects `1.5`, `-1` or `7`. Concrete failures: (a) a float or out-of-range index makes `index === questions[i].correctAnswerIndex` (QuizModal.tsx:78,183) and `index === current.correctAnswerIndex` (ReviewPage.tsx:76,94) false for every option — the quiz marks every answer wrong, shows no correct answer, and reports 0%; the same wrong index is persisted into the `ReviewCard` at QuizModal.tsx:52-61 and mis-grades that card forever. (b) `options` has no `minItems`, so an empty array renders a question with zero buttons (QuizModal.tsx:182); `isAnswered` can never become true, and the 'Next Question' button at QuizModal.tsx:242 stays `disabled` — the modal soft-locks with no way forward except closing it. Correct fix: `Type.INTEGER` with `minimum: 0`/`maximum: 3`, `minItems: '4'`/`maxItems: '4'` on `options`, plus a runtime bounds check in quiz.ts before persisting. Blast radius: QUIZ_SCHEMA is the only shape enforcement for both QuizModal and every ReviewCard ever created.

findings.title: `category` is an unconstrained STRING in the schema, a plain `string` in TS, and the allowed list exists only in prompt prose
findings.description: Three layers disagree about what a category is. The Gemini schema declares `category: { type: Type.STRING }` with no `enum` and no `format: 'enum'`, even though `Schema.enum?: string[]` exists (genai.d.ts:12051). The allowed values live only as prose in prompts.ts:12 ('The category should be one of: Psychology, Productivity, Business, Technology, Philosophy, Health, Biography, Other'), which is a suggestion the model can ignore. `Book.category` (src/types.ts:33) is `string`. And src/types.ts:6-15 declares a `Category` enum with exactly those eight values that is imported and used nowhere in the codebase — dead code that documents an invariant nothing enforces. Failure: the model returns 'Self-Help' or 'Personal Development'; it is accepted, persisted, and LibraryPage.tsx:65 builds the category filter chips from `new Set(books.map(b => b.category))`, so the filter bar accretes near-duplicate one-book categories over time and StatsView's category breakdown fragments. Nothing crashes — this is silent data-quality drift the type system was in a position to prevent. Correct fix: add `enum` + `format: 'enum'` to the schema, change `Book['category']` to a literal union derived from the existing `Category` enum (or delete the enum), and coerce unknown values to 'Other' at the parse boundary — summarize.ts:26 already has the `|| 'Other'` fallback, it just never fires for a non-empty wrong string.

findings.title: `rating` and `readingTimeMinutes` carry their ranges only in description text and are persisted unvalidated
findings.description: Both are `Type.NUMBER` with the intended range stated only in a `description` — 'A rating from 1 to 5' and 'Estimated time in minutes... assume 250 words per minute'. `Schema.minimum`/`Schema.maximum` (genai.d.ts:12064,12072) are available and unused, and `Book.rating` / `Book.readingTimeMinutes` (src/types.ts:36,47) are unbranded `number`s, so neither layer rejects 8.7, -3 or 100000. summarize.ts:28-29 applies only `?? 0` / `?? 5`, which fire on nullish values, not out-of-range ones. AddBookModal.tsx:74 happens to overwrite `rating` with the user's slider value, but LibraryPage.tsx:90-94 (the 'add from recommendation' path) persists the model's number verbatim. Failure: BookCard.tsx:100 renders `{book.rating}/5` producing '8.7/5'; BookDetail.tsx:278-287 renders a five-star row via `num <= Math.round(book.rating)` so a rating of 8.7 lights every star and prints '8.7' beside them; StatsView.tsx:20 averages ratings across finished books and reports a skewed average forever. No crash, but permanently wrong displayed data with no correction path for the rating that came from the recommendation flow. Correct fix: `minimum`/`maximum` in the schema plus a clamp at the parse boundary — the natural home is `toGenerated` in summarize.ts, which already normalises every other field.

findings.title: sendMessageStream returns `Promise<string>` that is silently empty on a blocked completion, leaving a permanently blank chat bubble
findings.description: `chunk.text` is `string | undefined` in the SDK (genai.d.ts:9465) and line 33 coalesces it to `''`. If the model produces no text at all — a safety block on the reply, an immediately-truncated stream, or an empty candidate list — the loop completes without throwing and the function returns `''`. The return type `Promise<string>` cannot express that difference, so callers have no compiler-visible reason to handle it. ChatModal.tsx:59 pushes a placeholder `{ role: 'model', text: '' }` before the call, `onChunk` is never invoked so the placeholder is never filled, and the recovery code at ChatModal.tsx:70-79 lives in a `catch` that never fires. The user sees an empty assistant bubble that stays empty, with no error toast and no retry affordance. The catch block is even written to replace a model message whose `text === ''` (line 75) — the exact state produced here — so the intended handling exists but is unreachable on this path. Correct shape: throw an `AiError` (errors.ts already defines the `'safety'` kind and its copy at errors.ts:33) when the accumulated text is empty, or return a tagged result the caller must destructure. Blast radius: 1 call site (ChatModal.tsx:61).

findings.title: The audio part's mimeType is discarded and the PCM format is hardcoded, so a format change produces silently corrupt WAV
findings.description: Line 27 reaches into `response.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.inlineData?.data` and takes only `data`. The sibling `inlineData.mimeType` — which Gemini TTS populates with the actual format descriptor, e.g. `audio/L16;codec=pcm;rate=24000` — is never read. `pcmToWavBlob` (src/lib/audio/wav.ts:1-3,12) hardcodes SAMPLE_RATE 24000, NUM_CHANNELS 1, BITS_PER_SAMPLE 16 and stamps those into the RIFF header at wav.ts:22-27. Nothing at any layer checks that the bytes actually match: `base64ToBytes` returns `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` for any decodable input and the header is written unconditionally. If a model revision returns a different sample rate or channel count, the WAV header lies about the payload and the audio plays at the wrong pitch and speed — a silent wrong-output failure, not an exception, and the blob is then persisted to the `blobs` store and replayed from cache. The declared parameter type `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` describes the container but carries no information about the encoding it must be, which is exactly the case for a branded/validated boundary. Correct fix: read `mimeType` alongside `data`, parse the `rate=` and `codec=` parameters, and either pass them into `pcmToWavBlob` or throw an `AiError` of kind `'malformed'` when they differ from what the WAV writer assumes. Verified positive worth recording: line 28's `if (!base64Audio) throw` correctly narrows the SDK's optional chain instead of using `!` — this file contains no non-null assertion. Blast radius: 2 call sites (BookDetail.tsx:159, EReader.tsx:203).

findings.title: User-controlled book titles are interpolated raw into the prompt that defines the requested output shape
findings.description: `recommendationsPrompt(booksList)` embeds a string that recommend.ts:20-22 builds from `b.title`, `b.author` and `b.category` for every book in the library, unescaped and unlength-capped. Those values are not app-authored: the Goodreads CSV importer writes them verbatim from a file the user supplies, and `Book.title`/`author`/`category` are plain `string` (src/types.ts:31-33) with no branding separating 'text safe to interpolate into a prompt' from 'arbitrary imported text'. The same pattern applies at prompts.ts:24 (detailedSummaryPrompt), :45 (quizPrompt), :56 (chatSystemInstruction) and :81 (audioScript), which additionally interpolate `summary.summary` and `summary.keyInsights` — themselves prior model output. Because line 41 asks in prose for 'strictly JSON with an array of objects containing title, author, and a 1-sentence description', a crafted title can restate or contradict that instruction and steer the response shape; combined with L05-F04's unvalidated cast, a steered response reaches the consumer as a typed `Recommendation[]`. This is adjacent to prompt injection but its type-safety consequence is concrete: the codebase treats a string that controls a request's output contract as interchangeable with a display string. Correct fix shape: escape or fence interpolated library values (and cap their length) in the prompt builders, and keep the runtime validation at the parse site as the real defence. Verified negative worth recording: prompts.ts is otherwise clean — every export has inferred-string return types from template literals, no assertions, no non-null assertions, and the `type: 'short' | 'long'` parameter at line 79 is a proper literal union. Blast radius: 5 prompt builders, all 6 AI entry points.
